title: Social inequality of test results and primary-school segregation
title_hu: A teszteredmények társadalmi egyenlőtlensége és az általános iskolai szegregáció
summary_en: How much of Hungarian primary-school test-score inequality is between-school (i.e., school-segregation-driven) vs. within-school? Hermann, Kertesi and Varga decompose Hungarian primary-school test-score variance using OKM and KIR data and document that between-school variance accounts for an unusually large share of total inequality compared with OECD peers. The chapter pinpoints the school-allocation mechanisms (free choice, six-year-gymnasium selection at age 10, religious-school exit) that drive the elevated between-school component.
policy_relevance: Foundational input for Hungarian education-equity policy (BM Köznevelési Stratégia, OFI): supports policy levers that compress the between-school component — restricted free-choice in segregated districts, later track allocation, integration-bonus funding for receiving schools. Quantifies the equity cost of Hungarian-specific institutional choices in a way that is directly comparable to OECD PISA equity rankings.
